chat.author: Robert Wilton
chat.text: Agreed that the YANG module needs to be there.  But I don't know if you need say any more than that or use 2119 language.  The text is normative regardless of whether 2119 statements are used.

chat.author: Per Andersson
chat.text: It was raised in a review that either yang library or capabilities need to be authorative. IMO it is unecessary because both are just there. Should the text about discovery just be removed in your opinion? I'm fine with that.

chat.author: Kent Watsen
chat.text: NC-next and RC-next may obsolete their redundant mechanisms

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: Thanks @Reshad for bringing up the implementation question.

chat.author: Robert Wilton
chat.text: Re: Per.  Yes, I don't think you need to make either authoritative.  An implementation needs to publish both to be consistent.

chat.author: Robert Wilton
chat.text: Also agree with Kent that NC-next and RC-next may obsolete these mechanisms and just use YANG library.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text:
This is not in a RFC (as yet) but in draft-ietf-masque-quic-proxy, Section 1 says - "QUIC long header packets between clients and targets MUST be proxied in tunnelled mode. QUIC short header packets between clients and targets MAY be proxied in forwarded mode, subject to negotiation between a client and a proxy."
I am not sure if you response (from the controller) is long or not.
